name: tag-179
iocPatterns: Wevtutil usage for event log export
keyCapabilities: Remote command execution via Remcos backdoor
Network reconnaissance using ipconfig, arp, SharpNBTScan
Credential dumping from SAM hive and cleartext capture at Winlogon
Local file collection based on document extensions (.docx,.pdf,.pptx,etc.)
Data staging and local storage prior to exfiltration
Use of cmd.exe, PowerShell, WMI for discovery and exfiltration
Exploitation of CVE‑2019‑9081 and other Windows CVEs for arbitrary execution
recommendedActions: Block and monitor traffic to known C2 IPs such as 89.31.121.220.
Deploy signatures or anomaly detection for Remcos backdoor communication.
Monitor for abnormal ipconfig/arp/SharpNBTScan activity indicating reconnaissance.
Restrict and detect use of wevtutil, certutil, cmd.exe, PowerShell, and WMI for privileged data export. Implement endpoint detection to flag credential dumping against the SAM hive or from Winlogon.
Apply least privilege on user accounts to reduce credential exposure.

Patch systems for CVE‑2019‑9081 and all referenced Windows security updates. Enforce network controls and IPS signatures to detect/block DDoS traffic initiated by infected hosts. Detect cryptojacking via abnormal CPU usage or known mining binaries and throttle or isolate affected machines.
campaignsText: TAG‑179 has exhibited a high operational tempo, with continuous activity from February 2024 through at least April 2026 in targeting Pakistani law‑enforcement entities. The actors repeatedly use the same Remcos CIDs and recurring IP addresses (e.g., 89.31.121.220) for command & control, indicating a well‑maintained supply chain. Victim types span across public sector institutions—law‑enforcement, government ministries, energy and telecom operators—showcasing preference for high‑value data in politically sensitive regions. Notable operations include the weaponised portals into Balochistan Police’s Complaint Management System and a series of cryptojacking campaigns that exploited CVE‑2019‑9081 to execute arbitrary code.
description: TAG-179 is a China- and India‑nexus cyber‑espionage group that has been operating against Pakistani law‑enforcement and public institutions since early 2024, primarily using the Remcos backdoor for remote persistence and data exfiltration. The actors employ credential dumping, network reconnaissance and document collection techniques to harvest information while leveraging existing CVE vulnerabilities and cryptojacking modules to add additional revenue streams. Their operational tempo has been consistent with periods of rapid exfiltration followed by lateral spread within targeted networks.
goals: TAG‑179’s primary objective is strategic espionage, focusing on gaining actionable intelligence from Pakistan’s law‑enforcement and public sector assets. By targeting agencies across a broad spectrum (government, defense, telecoms, energy, healthcare, finance, etc.), the group seeks to harvest information that supports geopolitical or military objectives for China and India respectively. Secondary goals include revenue generation through cryptojacking and DDoS campaigns, as well as establishing back‑door persistence to enable future operations on a wider range of critical infrastructures.
